title: Restructuring the Governance and Funding Model of the Consolidated Audit Trail
summary: Although the consolidated audit trail (the "CAT") continues to be a necessary regulatory tool, its decentralized governance has presented certain challenges to administering the CAT. To address those shortcomings, the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") proposes to assume direct control of the CAT. Specifically, the Commission is proposing amendments to Regulation NMS under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 ("Exchange Act") that would rescind Rule 613, which obligates the national securities exchanges and national securities associations (collectively, the "SROs") to act jointly to develop a national market system plan to develop, implement, and maintain the CAT (the "CAT NMS Plan"). The Commission is simultaneously proposing new Rule 17a-26, which would require the SROs and broker-dealers to record and electronically report to a central repository substantially the same information that was previously required to be recorded and reported pursuant to Rule 613, the CAT NMS Plan, related SRO compliance rules, and related exemptive relief previously issued by the Commission.

title: Loyalty and the Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights
summary: In this proposed rule, the Department of Labor (Department) clarifies the fiduciary duty of loyalty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). The proposed rule affirms that ERISA's duty of loyalty requires fiduciaries to act with the exclusive purpose of ensuring retirement security and providing promised benefits to plan participants and their beneficiaries. The amendments clarify the neutral application of ERISA's fiduciary duties of prudence and loyalty to selecting investments and investment courses of action, and to exercising shareholder rights, including proxy voting, the use of written proxy voting policies and guidelines, and shareholder engagement activities. The amendments would enhance the regulation by adding an affirmative expression of the duty of loyalty that is more consistent with the statute, and removing the tiebreaker test and participant preference provisions, which do not comport with the best reading of the statute and are susceptible to abuse, including use by a fiduciary as pretext to employ plan assets to pursue personal preferences or objectives unrelated to financial benefits under the plan. In the Department's view, the best reading of ERISA's exclusive purpose provision is and has always been that a plan fiduciary may not start with an ulterior motive or consider any factors collateral to plan participants' financial interests during any part of the process of making investment-selection decisions. The proposal would strengthen the fiduciary standards of pension and retirement plans covered by ERISA as instructed in President Trump's Executive Order 14366, Protecting American Investors from Foreign-Owned and Politically Motivated Proxy Advisors.

title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-21- 08, which applied to certain The Boeing Company Model 737-700, -700C, - 800, and -900ER series airplanes. AD 2026-21-08 required a detailed inspection of the left- and right-side form-in-place (FiP) gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for correct sealant installation, a fluid leak test of the engine fuel shutoff valve access panels for any leak, and applicable on-condition actions. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-21-08, the FAA has determined that the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of AD 2026-21-08 omits reference to a certain date. This AD retains all of the requirements of AD 2026- 21-08 and adds the omitted reference to the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of this AD. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Streamlining the Application Process for Grants for Adaptive Sports Programs for Disabled Veterans and Disabled Members of the Armed Forces
summary: This proposed rule would amend the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regulations that govern grants for adaptive sports programs for disabled veterans and disabled members of the armed forces to allow for a more efficient review and selection of applicants for the grant. This rule would ensure that the grant aligns with the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards by requiring applicants to submit an application within the VA established deadline for submission; requiring that all adaptive sports grants be openly competed; and adding a new section on appropriate actions VA may take to enforce this part. The changes proposed by this rulemaking will improve program administration without negatively impacting the veteran athletes supported by these grants.

title: Streamlining and Improving Efficiencies in the RCRA Hazardous Waste Permitting Program; Notice of Virtual Public Meetings and Request for Information
summary: This document announces and initiates an EPA effort to streamline the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) permit program and to remove associated barriers to redevelopment. This effort will satisfy an Agency Priority Goal established by the EPA Administrator to streamline the permitting process and improve efficiencies to unleash economic growth. In this document, EPA seeks information to help identify inefficiencies in the permit process and ideas for streamlining, including ideas that would reduce the time, uncertainty, and costs involved in issuing a permit. EPA also seeks information to help identify situations where the RCRA permit presents barriers to redevelopment of and/or parceling of RCRA treatment, storage, and disposal facilities, and ideas to overcome those barriers. EPA will consider information submitted as it develops a plan to address the inefficiencies in, and barriers presented by, the current RCRA permit program. This document also announces four virtual public engagement sessions that will supplement the request for information by providing individual participants an opportunity to provide oral comments on these issues as well.
